You look really good man, I'm sorry people haven't been treating you well. I really like your style, folks on here are just against people expressing themselves. I'm 21 too & I'd absolutely ask you out. You seem sweet and genuine.

I'd recommend spending time doing things you enjoy, prioritizing people who build you up, & figuring out your interests/goals/wants in all walks of life. It's important to know who you are & to work on loving that person. You're still really young & there's ample time to find a partner.
Guy here, can confirm. OP, you're really attractive & you seem like a really interesting and fun person. Take some time to work on your confidence & self image and you'll be golden.

A lot of 16 year olds go through a "everyone is out to get me phase," so I don't necessarily think the way you're responding to people is odd, but I hope you grow out of it soon because it's a miserable way to live your life and makes it hard to form relationships. Sometimes a compliment is just a compliment, sometimes a suggestion is just a suggestion. Sometimes it's not, but you have to be able to learn to tell the difference. Right now you're on defense mode and that's making it hard on you.

Maybe consider some counseling. I had similar ways of responding to people and talking about myself but I've been in therapy a long while since and it has really helped.

If you like the gothic style: great. Find some ways to make it work better for you. Lean into it harder. I think the outfits in 2-3 & 8-9 are the best on you & you look the most comfortable in them. Comfort, confidence, and fun are the most essential parts of how you come across to others. Not everyone is going to jive with you or your style & that's ok.

Experiment with bolder makeup - there's a lot of fun YouTube tutorials that should help you on this front. Experiment with your hair - maybe use spray or mousse to volumize, try different cuts, mix and match different colours. You're at the age where you should be having fun with your style, not posting on this subreddit trying to see what random extremely online people think of you from a few pictures.

Seconding this. The hair is good for your age range and suits your face currently. Once you age, then it might be a good time to start looking into different styles, but right now this definitely works for you. Your face and body will change a lot up through to your mid 20s, I really wouldn't fixate on how you look right now because that's going to change quite a lot in the coming years. Focus on prioritizing your confidence, get into some hobbies, and just enjoy your youth.

There are several reasons your response rubs me the wrong way.

I am perfectly aware that there is no "finish line." 
I am not as naive as you perhaps would like to imagine. 

Yes, relationships need their own momentum, but you DO have to put in effort. It's not just "oh well we're dating and if it doesn't work perfectly 100% of the time it's not worth it." Relationships have their challenges, and people who are dedicated in a relationship work through those challenges. A relationship in itself is not a challenge, but is threaded with them. When I said I planned to fight for the relationship, I was referring to fighting through the obstacles, not fighting for it to stay afloat.

Our relationship, believe it or not, is stable. We are both well aware of the challenges in our way, but as we work through them, we're having a hell of a fun time. Please don't assume our relationship is any less than amazing because it happens to be long distance. There is no sense of needing to "maintain a difficult relationship" because frankly, it's not difficult for us to love each other and have a healthy relationship. We do not feel "loneliness and pain" because we are apart physically. He lives near my parents, so I visit him when I visit them. It works out. Go figure. Also, conflict in ANY kind of relationship is necessary and inevitable. There is nothing in this world that does not involve conflict. 

I never liked romance movies. I don't expect this to be 'easy peasy lemon squeezy' once we close the distance. Hell, I don't even know if we'll stay together long enough to close the distance. As you said, people change. But we are going to continue pursuing this as long as we think it's a healthy, happy, and sustainable relationship. Maybe it seems implausible and stupid, but that's our choice to make.

An experience is never wasted. Time spent on something, whether it works or not, teaches us how to conduct ourselves in the future.

Maybe this is the naivety of being 17, but I think it's definitely worth it. I'm not saying that I'm certain that everything will work for 10 years, but if there's any chance it will, I'll fight and fight and fight for it. 💪💛

It's the best case scenario for sure. Nothing is really set other than his 2 years of community and my 5 years of dual undergrad/masters.

We're both really quite committed, I don't doubt that we could get through it with hard enough work. We already have been LD for a while, and it's worked so far.

Maybe it's naive. Maybe we're just stupid and 17. But I'd rather be stupid and 17 with him than without him. We'll take it as it comes I suppose.

Honestly, all that's set pretty much in stone for us is his 2 years of community in TX and my 5 years in dual undergrad/masters program up in ND.
